Saturated pixels in the W51 JWST images: what kinds there are, how many, and how each kind was restored¶

28 October 2026. JWST program 6151 (W51): NIRCam F182M and F410M, MIRI F560W, F770W, F1000W, F1280W and F2100W.

The story. W51 is one of the brightest star-forming regions in the Galaxy, and its brightest parts saturated the JWST detectors: they collected more light than a pixel can record. The pipeline gives many of those pixels no value, so the images have holes. Saturated pixels differ in how much information the detector still kept about them: some lost only their last reads, some lost all of them. That difference decides which restoration method can work. This notebook

  1. defines five kinds of saturated pixels by what the detector kept (section 1),
  2. shows where each kind sits in real images (section 2),
  3. counts each kind in every filter (section 3),
  4. shows which method restored each kind, and how accurate each method is (section 4),
  5. shows how many sky pixels are still empty after the exposures are combined (section 5),
  6. lists what is left, kind by kind (section 6).

Number tables are in the appendix. The methods themselves are described in detail in report_restoration_20261027.ipynb.

How a JWST detector records a pixel¶

During an exposure each pixel collects electric charge from the light that falls on it. The detector reads that charge several times without emptying the pixel, a scheme called "up the ramp". The growth from read to read gives the pixel's brightness.

  • NIRCam (readout pattern SHALLOW2): 5 reads, 53.7 s apart. Each read (a "group") is the average of 2 frames. The very first frame, read 10.7 s after the start, is also kept: the first read (ZEROFRAME). It collected light for half as long as the first group.
  • MIRI (readout pattern FASTR1): 5 reads, 2.8 s apart.

A pixel can hold only so much charge. Above a flag threshold the pipeline marks a read as saturated and does not use it. The recorded signal still creeps up a little above the threshold, until it reaches the detector's hard ceiling, where it stays flat. The pipeline computes the brightness from the reads before saturation. A pixel with no good read gets no value.

Glossary¶

term meaning
read, group one non-destructive reading of a pixel during the exposure (5 per exposure here)
good read a read below the flag threshold, which the pipeline uses
first read (ZEROFRAME) NIRCam only: the single first frame, after 10.7 s
flag threshold the signal above which the pipeline flags a read as saturated
hard ceiling the largest signal the detector can record; a pixel at the ceiling gives no information
exposure, dither one image; the 16-64 exposures per filter are shifted slightly ("dithered"), so a sky position falls on different pixels
pixel-exposure one pixel in one exposure; all counts in sections 1-4 are of pixel-exposures
sky pixel one pixel of the combined image (mosaic) of all exposures (section 5)
dex a factor in log10: 0.01 dex = 2.3%, 0.1 dex = 26%
response curve how MIRI's recorded signal grows with the collected charge above the flag threshold; inverted to read the charge back
star model a fit of the known star shape (point-spread function) to the unsaturated wings of a star
cross-filter fill a prediction of a pixel from its brightness in other filters (a censored fit); for F2100W pinned to SOFIA
SOFIA an airborne telescope image of W51 at 19.7 um with 3" resolution, which does not saturate
census the table of every saturated pixel-exposure, with its saturation level and type (census/pixels.parquet)

1. Five kinds of saturated pixels¶

What a method can do with a saturated pixel depends on how much the detector kept. Figure 1 shows the reads of one pixel of each of the first four kinds (toy numbers): the grey dashed line is the charge the light delivers, the dots are what the detector recorded.

In [2]:
thr, ceil = 1.0, 1.12
recorded = lambda q: np.where(q < thr, q, ceil - (ceil - thr) * np.exp(-(q - thr) / 0.25))   # toy detector
cases = [('late', 0.28), ('one', 0.75), ('first', 1.25), ('ceiling', 4.0)]   # charge per read
caption = {'late': 'the pipeline fits the good reads:\nits value is fine',
           'one': 'one good read: the pipeline value\nexists (MIRI: corrected for a bias)',
           'first': 'the first read is above the flag but below\nthe ceiling: it still measures the charge',
           'ceiling': 'flat at the ceiling from the first read:\nthe pixel itself tells nothing'}
reads, tt = np.arange(1, 6), np.linspace(0, 5.4, 200)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(18, 5.4), sharey=True)
for ax, (k, rate) in zip(axes, cases):
    q = rate * reads
    good = q < thr
    ax.plot(tt, rate * tt, color=GREY, ls='--', lw=1.3)
    ax.plot(reads[good], recorded(q[good]), 'o', color=BLUE, ms=9)
    ax.plot(reads[~good], recorded(q[~good]), 'o', mfc='white', mec=ORANGE, mew=2, ms=9)
    ax.axhline(thr, color=ORANGE, lw=1, ls=':'); ax.axhline(ceil, color=INK, lw=1.2)
    ax.set_title(KLAB[k].replace(', below', ',\nbelow'), fontsize=11.5)
    ax.set_xticks(reads); ax.set_xlabel('read'); ax.set_xlim(0, 5.5); ax.set_ylim(0, 1.45)
    ax.text(0.5, -0.22, caption[k], transform=ax.transAxes, ha='center', va='top', fontsize=10.5, color=INK)
axes[0].set_yticks([0, 0.5, thr, ceil], ['0', '0.5', 'flag threshold', 'hard ceiling'])
axes[0].set_ylabel('recorded signal')
fig.legend(handles=[plt.Line2D([], [], color=GREY, ls='--', lw=1.3, label='charge the light delivers'),
                    plt.Line2D([], [], color=BLUE, marker='o', ls='', ms=9, label='good read'),
                    plt.Line2D([], [], color=ORANGE, marker='o', mfc='white', mew=2, ls='', ms=9, label='flagged read')],
           loc='upper center', ncol=3, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.02), fontsize=10.5)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.08, right=0.99, top=0.8, bottom=0.3, wspace=0.08)
kind what the exposure kept how it is identified in the data what it still tells us
1. saturated late 2 or more good reads the first saturated read is read 3, 4 or 5 (census sat_level ≥ 2) the brightness, from the good reads: the pipeline value is fine
2. one good read exactly one good read the first saturated read is read 2 (sat_level = 1) the brightness from one read. In MIRI that value comes out 0.057 dex too low on average and is corrected
3. saturated in the first read, below the ceiling no good read, but a first reading below the hard ceiling MIRI: the first read is below the ceiling (ramp class 2-3); NIRCam: the first frame is below the threshold (types A-soft, B, C) the collected charge, from the first reading: MIRI through the response curve, NIRCam from the first frame
4. at the ceiling from the first read nothing: every read is at the ceiling MIRI ramp class 4; NIRCam type A-hard (the first frame is saturated too) nothing in the pixel itself. The value has to come from elsewhere: the shape of a star, or the other filters
5. no usable reading a reading that cannot be used bad pixel, hot pixel or cosmic ray, a pixel without a flat field (outside the calibrated sky), or a MIRI coronagraph-pane pixel the response curve does not cover nothing in this exposure; other exposures, or the other filters (coronagraph panes)

Two more facts matter for the counts:

  • Neighbours. The pipeline also flags the 8 neighbours of a saturated pixel, because charge can spill over. Some of these neighbours never reached the threshold themselves. They are part of kind 3 ("neighbour" below) and their first reading is usually fine.
  • Kinds are per exposure. The exposures are dithered, so one sky position can be kind 4 in one exposure and kind 2 in another, where it fell on a different pixel or between pixels. Section 5 shows how much this helps.
  • Star or extended. Each saturated area is marked as a star (a compact source that the star model can fit) or as extended emission (W51's bright gas and dust, too large for a star fit). The method depends on this for kinds 3 and 4.

2. Where the kinds sit in an image¶

Figure 2 shows three real cases, one per row: the brightest F2100W core in one MIRI exposure, the brightest F410M core in one NIRCam exposure, and the brightest star in one F182M exposure. Left: the restored image (orange: still empty). Middle: the kind of each saturated pixel. Right: the method that gave its value.

In [3]:
KI = {k: i for i, k in enumerate(KINDS)}
OI = {o: i for i, o in enumerate(OUTS)}

def maps(F, name):
    # kind index (-1 unsaturated) and outcome index (-1 unsaturated) of every pixel of one exposure, and its image
    g = sk.census(F, name)
    kind, sub, out = sk.classify(F, name, g)
    sci = fits.getdata(f'{FIN}/{F}/{name}_restored.fits', 'SCI')
    K = np.full(sci.shape, -1); O = np.full(sci.shape, -1)
    K[g.y.values, g.x.values] = [KI[k] for k in kind]
    O[g.y.values, g.x.values] = [OI[o] for o in out]
    return sci, K, O, g, kind, sub

def centre(K, want, half, x0=0):
    # the window with the most pixels of kind `want` (MIRI: right of the coronagraph columns, x0)
    d = ndimage.uniform_filter((K == KI[want]).astype(float), 2 * half)
    d[:half], d[-half:], d[:, :x0 + half], d[:, -half:] = 0, 0, 0, 0   # keep the window on the detector
    return np.unravel_index(np.argmax(d), d.shape)

def f182m_star():
    # the F182M exposure and star with the most ceiling pixels
    c = sk.census('F182M')
    c = c[(c.sat_level == 0) & (c.l0_type == 'A-hard') & (c.region >= 1)]
    return c.groupby(['file', 'region']).size().idxmax()[0]

kcmap = ListedColormap(['white'] + [KCOL[k] for k in KINDS])
ocmap = ListedColormap(['white'] + [OCOL[o] for o in OUTS])
rows = [('F2100W', 'jw06151002001_02109_00001_mirimage', 'ceiling', 90, 'MIRI F2100W core'),
        ('F410M', 'jw06151001001_03107_00001_nrcalong', 'ceiling', 45, 'NIRCam F410M core'),
        ('F182M', f182m_star(), 'ceiling', 22, 'NIRCam F182M star')]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(16, 16))
used_o = set()
for ax, (F, name, want, half, title) in zip(axes, rows):
    sci, K, O, g, kind, sub = maps(F, name)
    cy, cx = centre(K, want, half, x0=365 if F in sk.MIRI else 0)
    sl = (slice(max(cy - half, 0), cy + half), slice(max(cx - half, 0), cx + half))
    img = sci[sl]
    v = np.nanpercentile(img, [2, 99.8])
    cm = plt.get_cmap('magma').copy(); cm.set_bad(ORANGE)
    ax[0].imshow(img, origin='lower', cmap=cm, norm=LogNorm(max(v[0], 1e-2), v[1]), interpolation='nearest')
    ax[1].imshow(K[sl] + 1, origin='lower', cmap=kcmap, vmin=-0.5, vmax=len(KINDS) + 0.5, interpolation='nearest')
    ax[2].imshow(O[sl] + 1, origin='lower', cmap=ocmap, vmin=-0.5, vmax=len(OUTS) + 0.5, interpolation='nearest')
    used_o |= {OUTS[i] for i in np.unique(O[sl]) if i >= 0}
    ax[0].set_title(f'{title}: restored image'); ax[1].set_title('kind'); ax[2].set_title('method')
    for a in ax:
        a.set_xticks([]); a.set_yticks([]); a.grid(False)
fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=KCOL[k], ec=GREY, label=KLAB[k]) for k in KINDS] + [Patch(fc='white', ec=GREY, label='not saturated')],
           title='kind', loc='lower left', bbox_to_anchor=(0.02, -0.02), ncol=2, fontsize=10)
fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=OCOL[o], ec=GREY, label=OLAB[o]) for o in OUTS if o in used_o],
           title='method', loc='lower right', bbox_to_anchor=(0.99, -0.02), ncol=2, fontsize=10)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.02, right=0.99, top=0.97, bottom=0.12, wspace=0.04, hspace=0.12)

Reading the figure. The kinds form rings, because the brightness rises towards the centre of a core or a star. The outer ring saturated late (kind 1, lightest), the next ring after one read (kind 2), then come the pixels that saturated in their first read but stayed below the ceiling (kind 3), and the centre sits at the ceiling (kind 4, darkest). The method map follows the rings: the pipeline value outside, the corrected value and the response curve (MIRI) or the first read and star model (NIRCam) in between, and the cross-filter fill or the star model at the centre.

  • MIRI F2100W: the response curve (blue) covers a wide ring around the core, and the cross-filter fill (orange) the core itself. Grey pixels have no flat field; the small dark-red spot is a core pixel without a usable input filter.
  • NIRCam F410M: the core is filled from the other filters (orange, and light orange for the low-confidence set); its darkest part stays empty (dark red). A thin dark-red ring separates the filled core from the pipeline values: pixels next to a ceiling pixel, whose first read holds spilled charge, and pixels the pipeline marked "do not use" (section 6). In the image these show as thin orange outlines.
  • NIRCam F182M star: the star model (yellow) fills the centre, with a few first-read pixels (green) at its edge.

3. How many saturated pixels of each kind, per filter¶

Figure 3 counts every saturated pixel-exposure of each filter (the total is at the right of each bar) and splits it by kind.

In [4]:
k = t.pivot_table(index='filter', columns='kind', values='n', aggfunc='sum').fillna(0).reindex(FILTERS)[KINDS]
share = 100 * k.div(k.sum(axis=1), axis=0)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 5))
left = np.zeros(len(share))
for kd in KINDS:
    ax.barh(share.index, share[kd], left=left, color=KCOL[kd], edgecolor='white', linewidth=1.5, label=KLAB[kd])
    for i, (l, v) in enumerate(zip(left, share[kd])):
        if v >= 4:
            ax.text(l + v / 2, i, f'{v:.0f}%', ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9.5, color='white' if kd == 'ceiling' else INK)
    left += share[kd].values
for i, n in enumerate(k.sum(axis=1)):
    ax.text(101, i, f'{n / 1e6:.2f} M' if n >= 1e6 else f'{n / 1e3:,.0f} k', va='center', fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
ax.set_xlim(0, 109); ax.invert_yaxis(); ax.grid(axis='y', visible=False)
ax.set_xlabel('saturated pixel-exposures of the filter (%)')
ax.legend(loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.45, -0.15), ncol=3, fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()

Reading the figure.

  • Most saturated pixels kept good reads. Kinds 1 and 2 are 66-97% of the saturated pixel-exposures in every filter. Their pipeline value exists. Only MIRI's one-good-read pixels need a small correction.
  • Pixels with no good read (kinds 3-5) are 3% (F410M) to 12% (F182M) in NIRCam, and 13% (F770W) to 34% (F2100W) in MIRI. These are the pixels that need restoring.
  • The hard cases, at the ceiling (kind 4), grow with wavelength in MIRI: 0.6% in F770W, 2.5% in F1000W, 3.1% in F1280W, 7.1% in F2100W. W51's bright cores emit most at long wavelengths. In NIRCam they are 1.1% (F182M, all stars) and 1.6% (F410M, mostly extended cores).
  • Kind 5 is mostly not sky. In MIRI it is 6-12%: pixels without a flat field (the detector edge and the strips beside the coronagraph panes), which the pipeline flags as saturated but which never carry a value, plus up to 1.3% coronagraph-pane pixels (real sky). In NIRCam it is bad pixels, hot pixels and cosmic rays: 9% in F182M, 0.6% in F410M.
  • Stars and extended emission. In F182M and F560W every saturated area is a star. In F410M 72% of the saturated pixels are extended emission, and in F770W-F2100W 63-95%.

4. Which method restored each kind¶

Each saturated pixel takes its value from the first method in this list that applies (py/merge_restored.py). The code is the value stored in the METHOD layer of the restored files.

code method how it works used for kind accuracy
0 pipeline value the pipeline's fit to the good reads 1, 2 (NIRCam) as unsaturated pixels
1 pipeline value, corrected MIRI one-read values lack the charge collected before the first read; corrected from pixels with 2-4 good reads 2 (MIRI) 0.005-0.015 dex
2 first read NIRCam's single first frame, when it is below the threshold and not next to a ceiling pixel (which spills charge into it) 3 (NIRCam) about 0.02 dex
3 response curve MIRI: invert the measured relation between collected charge and recorded signal above the flag threshold, using the first read 3 (MIRI), up to 3x the threshold charge 0.003-0.03 dex
4 response curve, less reliable the same, 3-4.5x the threshold charge 3 (MIRI) 0.025-0.04 dex
5 star model fit the known star shape to the unsaturated wings of the star 3, 4 in stars (NIRCam) 0.11 dex per pixel; star totals to 0.006 dex
7 star model, low confidence the same where the model itself is uncertain 3, 4 in stars star totals 0.03 dex too bright
6 cross-filter fill predict the pixel from its brightness in the other filters with a censored fit; MIRI F2100W pinned to SOFIA 4 in extended emission; MIRI coronagraph panes MIRI: 0.07-0.09 dex at core edges, many core pixels are lower limits; F410M: +0.02-0.03 dex
9 cross-filter fill, low confidence the same from a filter set that failed its accept test 4 in F410M's brightest cores -0.04 dex, scatter 0.2 dex
8 not restored no method applies

Figure 4 shows, for each kind and subkind, which share of its pixels got which method (all filters of one instrument together; per-filter tables in the appendix).

In [5]:
SUBS = ['extended', 'star', 'neighbour', 'coronagraph panes', 'outside the calibrated sky', 'bad pixel', 'hot pixel or cosmic ray']
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(14, 14.5), gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[1, 1]))
for ax, inst in zip(axes, ['MIRI', 'NIRCam']):
    x = t[t.inst == inst].pivot_table(index=['kind', 'sub'], columns='outcome', values='n', aggfunc='sum').fillna(0)
    x = x.reindex(sorted(x.index, key=lambda r: (KINDS.index(r[0]), SUBS.index(r[1]))))
    cols = [o for o in OUTS if o in x.columns]
    x = x[cols]
    pct = 100 * x.div(x.sum(axis=1), axis=0)
    ax.imshow(pct.values, cmap='Purples', vmin=0, vmax=130, aspect='auto')
    for i in range(pct.shape[0]):
        for j in range(pct.shape[1]):
            v = pct.values[i, j]
            if v >= 0.5:
                ax.text(j, i, f'{v:.0f}%', ha='center', va='center', fontsize=9.5, color='white' if v > 70 else INK)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(pct)), [f'{KLAB[a].split(", below")[0]}: {b} ({int(n):,})' for (a, b), n in zip(pct.index, x.sum(axis=1))], fontsize=9.5)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(cols)), [OLAB[o] for o in cols], rotation=25, ha='right', fontsize=9.5)
    ax.set_title(f'{inst}: share of each kind restored by each method (pixel-exposures in brackets)')
    ax.grid(False)
    for i in range(1, len(pct)):
        if pct.index[i][0] != pct.index[i - 1][0]:
            ax.axhline(i - 0.5, color=INK, lw=0.8)
plt.tight_layout()

Reading the figure, kind by kind.

  • Kind 1, saturated late: the pipeline value, in 96-100% of the pixels. In NIRCam, 3-4% of these pixels in extended emission are not restored (and 1-2% in stars come from the star model). The pipeline marked them "do not use" although they kept good reads, so it gave them no value (section 6).
  • Kind 2, one good read: MIRI: the corrected pipeline value (99.9%). NIRCam: the pipeline value (97%), with the same exception as kind 1.
  • Kind 3, saturated in the first read: MIRI: the response curve for all of them, 78% within its best range (code 3) and 22% beyond 3x the threshold charge (code 4). NIRCam: in stars mostly the star model (83%), and the first read (16%); neighbour-flagged pixels the star model (63%) and the first read (28%). In extended emission the first read (36%); the other 64% sit next to a ceiling pixel, whose spilled charge makes the first read too bright, and stay empty.
  • Kind 4, at the ceiling: MIRI extended cores: the cross-filter fill (98.5%). MIRI stars (F560W): the low-confidence star model. NIRCam stars: the star model (78%, 22% low confidence). F410M cores: the cross-filter fill (35%), its low-confidence version (49%) and 16% not restored.
  • Kind 5, no usable reading: MIRI coronagraph panes: the cross-filter fill (99.9%). Pixels without a flat field and NIRCam bad pixels, hot pixels and cosmic rays: no value in that exposure. Other exposures cover their sky.

5. After combining the exposures: sky pixels still empty¶

A sky position is only empty in the final image if it is empty in every exposure that covers it. Figure 5 counts the sky pixels saturated in every exposure, before restoration (grey) and still empty after it (dark).

In [6]:
rows = []
for f in FILTERS:
    with fits.open(f'{FIN}/mosaic_{f}.fits') as h:
        a, b, m = h['AFTER'].data, h['BEFORE'].data, h['METHOD'].data
    sat = m >= 1
    rows.append(dict(filter=f, before=int((np.isnan(b) & sat).sum()), after=int((np.isnan(a) & sat).sum())))
holes = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index('filter')
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 4.6))
xx = np.arange(len(holes))
ax.bar(xx - 0.2, holes.before, 0.38, color=GREY, label='before: saturated in every exposure')
ax.bar(xx + 0.2, np.maximum(holes.after, 0.8), 0.38, color='#3f2378', label='after: still empty')
for i, (bv, av) in enumerate(zip(holes.before, holes.after)):
    ax.text(i - 0.2, bv * 1.15, f'{bv:,}', ha='center', fontsize=9.5)
    ax.text(i + 0.2, max(av, 0.8) * 1.15, f'{av:,}', ha='center', fontsize=9.5)
ax.set_yscale('log'); ax.set_ylim(0.5, 2e6)
ax.set_xticks(xx, holes.index); ax.set_ylabel('sky pixels of the mosaic'); ax.grid(axis='x', visible=False)
ax.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()
holes.assign(filled=(100 * (1 - holes.after / holes.before)).round(1).astype(str) + '%')

Reading the figure. Before restoration, W51's cores left 2,600-239,000 empty sky pixels per MIRI filter and 534-9,105 per NIRCam filter. After it, MIRI F560W has none left and F770W-F2100W have 200-610 each (98-100% filled). NIRCam F182M has 69 left (87% filled) and F410M 1,454 (84%). Many kind-5 pixels and single unrestored pixels vanish here, because another exposure measured the same sky.

6. What is left, kind by kind¶

  • NIRCam pixels with good reads but no pipeline value (kinds 1-2, about 42,000 pixel-exposures in extended emission). The pipeline marked early reads "do not use" (in the one F410M exposure checked, 45% of them already in the first read), so it gave them no value, although they kept 1-4 good reads. A rate fitted directly to their good reads could restore them. Not done yet.
  • NIRCam first reads next to a ceiling pixel (kind 3, about 4,800 in extended emission). Their first read contains charge spilled from the neighbour. A correction for the spill, or the cross-filter fill, could restore them.
  • Ceiling pixels without a usable filter (kind 4): 1.5% of MIRI's extended cores and 16% of F410M's, where a filter needed by the cross-filter fill is missing or saturated too.
  • Lower limits inside the MIRI cores (kind 4). Many filled core pixels sit at the floor, the smallest value a ceiling pixel can have: 97% in F770W, 96% in F1000W, 56% in F1280W, 19% in F2100W. Their true values are higher. Refitting F770W-F1280W as F2100W was refitted would reduce this.
  • Kind 5 stays empty in the exposure where it occurs. In the combined images other exposures cover most of it (section 5).

A3. How the kinds were assigned (py/saturation_kinds.py)

  • Every pixel flagged SATURATED in an exposure has one row in the census (census/pixels.parquet, 14.7 million rows over 15 filters; the 7 restored filters are used here).
  • sat_level is the number of good reads before the first saturated read (0: the first read is saturated already; -1: flagged without any saturated read, treated as kind 5).
  • MIRI kinds 3 and 4 come from the ramp step (production/miri_ramp/): class 2-3 (first read below the ceiling) and 4 (at the ceiling); class 5 (no usable reading) is kind 5. NIRCam kinds 3 and 4 come from the raw first read: type A-hard (the first frame at or above the threshold) is kind 4, types A-soft, B and C are kind 3.
  • The outcome is the METHOD code of the final restored file (production/final/<filter>/<exposure>_restored.fits) at the pixel. Code 0 is split into "pipeline value" and "no value" (a pixel outside the calibrated sky).
  • Consistency: 1,033 MIRI pixel-exposures (out of 9.6 million) are restored but not listed in the census, and about 4,100 MIRI pixel-exposures of kinds 1-2 got a response-curve value (the ramp step and the census disagree on their saturation level). Both are below 0.1% and are left as they are.

A4. Files. Counts: production/final/kinds/kinds_methods.csv. Restored images and mosaics: production/final/. Methods: report_restoration_20261027.ipynb.
